scientificReferences.title: Discovery and quantification of plastic particle pollution in human blood
scientificReferences.keyFinding: First quantifiable detection of microplastic polymers (<700 nm to 5 µm) in human bloodstream across 77% of tested donors. PET, polyethylene, and styrene polymers predominated.

scientificReferences.source: Hussain et al., Environmental Science & Technology (2023)
scientificReferences.title: Assessing Microplastic and Nanoplastic Release from Food Containers Under Everyday Use
scientificReferences.keyFinding: Microwave heating of polypropylene (PP) food containers releases up to 4.22 million microplastic and 2.11 billion nanoplastic particles per cm² within 3 minutes.

scientificReferences.title: Cutting Boards: An Overlooked Source of Microplastics in Human Food
scientificReferences.keyFinding: Daily chopping on polypropylene and polyethylene boards sheds 14.5 million to 50.4 million microplastic particles per person annually directly into chopped food.

scientificReferences.title: Re-evaluation of the risks to public health related to the presence of bisphenol A (BPA) in foodstuffs
scientificReferences.keyFinding: Lowered tolerable daily intake (TDI) of BPA to 0.2 ng/kg bw/day (20,000 times lower than previous benchmark) due to severe immune and endocrine toxicity.

polymerClasses.name: Polypropylene
polymerClasses.commonUses: Takeout food containers, microwave meal trays, reusable deli containers
polymerClasses.primaryRisks: Thermal polymer scission releasing billions of nanoplastics; cyclic polypropylene oligomers; catalyst residue migration.

polymerClasses.name: High/Low Density Polyethylene
polymerClasses.commonUses: Plastic chopping boards, squeeze bottles, sandwich zip bags
polymerClasses.primaryRisks: Mechanical blade shearing generates millions of microscopic fibrous shavings per slice; slip agents (erucamide/oleamide) leaching.

polymerClasses.name: Polyvinyl Chloride
polymerClasses.commonUses: Plastic cling film wrap, commercial food packaging, gasket seals
polymerClasses.primaryRisks: High concentrations of ortho-phthalate plasticizers (DEHP, DINP, DIDP) that migrate aggressively into lipophilic fatty foods.

polymerClasses.name: Polycarbonate & Blends
polymerClasses.commonUses: Vintage water jugs, blender carafes, food processor bowls
polymerClasses.primaryRisks: Hydrolytic cleavage of ester bonds releasing free monomeric Bisphenol A (BPA) and structural analogs (BPS, BPF).

polymerClasses.name: Polyethylene Terephthalate
polymerClasses.commonUses: Single-use beverage bottles, salad clamshells, condiment containers
polymerClasses.primaryRisks: Antimony trioxide catalyst leaching under warm ambient storage; nano-fragmentation upon repeated refilling or UV exposure.

polymerClasses.name: Melamine Formaldehyde Resin
polymerClasses.commonUses: Hard plastic dinnerware, toddler bowls, camping picnic sets
polymerClasses.primaryRisks: Release of free formaldehyde and melamine monomers at acidic pH or >70°C; linked to renal tubular damage and bladder calculi.

riskTiers.description: You encounter occasional polymer degradation, predominantly through plastic board cutting or infrequent microwave warming. Phthalate migration occurs during fatty food contact.

riskTiers.estimatedBloodBurden: Elevated polymer translocation risk (2.5–4.5 µg/mL equivalent)

riskTiers.estimatedBloodBurden: High biological accumulation potential (>5.0 µg/mL equivalent)

actionPlanInterventions.detail: Never heat any plastic container in the microwave, even those labeled 'microwave safe' (which only certifies the container won't melt, not that it won't leach billions of sub-micron particles). Transfer food to ceramic or borosilicate glass before pressing start.
actionPlanInterventions.recommendedProduct: Anchor Hocking or Pyrex 10-Piece Glass Food Storage Set with BPA-Free TrueSeal Lids

actionPlanInterventions.action: Swap Plastic Cutting Boards for End-Grain Hardwood
actionPlanInterventions.detail: Eliminates 15 to 50 million microscopic polyethylene/polypropylene shavings per year. Wood fibers naturally self-heal and harbor natural antimicrobial polyphenols that inhibit bacteria far better than scarred plastic.
actionPlanInterventions.recommendedProduct: John Boos Maple Edge-Grain Board or Organic Thick Acacia Cutting Block

actionPlanInterventions.action: Replace Plastic Electric Kettles with Seamless 316 Stainless Steel
actionPlanInterventions.detail: Repeated boiling in plastic kettles subjects polypropylene walls to continuous 100°C hydrolysis, infusing drinking water with dissolved plasticizers and micro-fragments.
actionPlanInterventions.recommendedProduct: Secura All-Stainless Steel Double-Wall Electric Kettle (Zero Plastic Food Contact)

actionPlanInterventions.action: Ditch PVC Cling Film for Beeswax Wraps & Unbleached Parchment
actionPlanInterventions.detail: Avoid covering warm or oily dishes directly with plastic cling wrap. Fatty oils draw lipophilic phthalates directly into cheese, meat, and leftover sauces.
actionPlanInterventions.recommendedProduct: Organic Cotton Beeswax Food Wraps (Pack of 7)
